title: From Anxious to Secure: Transforming Your Attachment Style
summary: A comprehensive seven-module CBT program designed to help you transform anxious attachment patterns into secure attachment. Learn to manage relationship anxiety, challenge core beliefs, regulate emotions, communicate needs effectively, and build the secure attachment style that leads to healthier, more fulfilling relationships.

modules.title: Module 1 • Understanding Anxious Attachment: The Foundation
modules.overview: Anxious attachment isn't a flaw—it's a learned pattern of relating that developed as a way to protect yourself. Understanding this pattern is the first step toward transforming it. This module helps you understand how anxious attachment develops, recognize its characteristics in your relationships, and see the path toward secure attachment. Knowledge is power. When you understand your attachment style, you can begin to change it. This module gives you that foundation.
takeaways: Anxious attachment is a learned pattern, not a character flaw—it can be changed.
Understanding your attachment style helps you recognize patterns and make different choices.
Secure attachment is achievable—many people successfully transform their attachment style.
Self-awareness is the first step: noticing your patterns without judgment.
exercises: Attachment style reflection: Write about your earliest memories of seeking comfort or attention. What patterns do you notice?
Pattern identification: List 5 behaviors or thoughts you have in relationships that might relate to anxious attachment.
Relationship timeline: Create a timeline of your significant relationships. What patterns do you see? How has anxious attachment shown up?
homework: Attachment journal: For one week, journal about your relationship thoughts and feelings. Notice when anxiety appears. What triggers it?
Pattern observation: This week, observe your anxious attachment patterns without judgment. Just notice. What do you see?
Secure attachment vision: Write about what secure attachment would look like for you. What would change? How would you feel?
Self-compassion practice: When you notice anxious patterns, practice self-compassion. 'This is a learned pattern. I'm learning to change it. That's okay.'

modules.title: Module 2 • Challenging Core Beliefs: Rewriting Your Relationship Blueprint
modules.overview: Core beliefs are the foundation of anxious attachment. Beliefs like 'I'm not worthy of love' or 'People always leave' drive anxious behaviors. This module teaches you to identify, challenge, and rewrite these beliefs. You'll learn cognitive restructuring techniques to replace anxious beliefs with secure ones. This isn't positive thinking—it's accurate thinking based on evidence. Changing beliefs changes behavior. When you believe you're worthy of stable love, you act differently. This module shows you how.
takeaways: Core beliefs drive anxious behaviors: change the beliefs, change the behaviors.
Beliefs are thoughts, not facts: you can challenge and change them.
Evidence-based thinking replaces anxious thinking: look for facts, not fears.
New beliefs need practice: repetition creates new patterns.
exercises: Belief identification: List 5 core beliefs you have about relationships. Which ones feel most true? Which cause the most anxiety?
Belief challenge: Choose one anxious belief. Challenge it. What's the evidence? What's an alternative view? Write it down.
Secure belief creation: Create 5 secure beliefs to replace anxious ones. Write them. Read them daily.
homework: Belief journal: This week, track your anxious beliefs. When do they appear? What triggers them? Challenge each one.
Thought record: Use a thought record to track: Situation, Thought, Feeling, Evidence for thought, Evidence against thought, Alternative thought, New feeling.
Belief replacement: When anxious beliefs appear, practice replacing them with secure ones. Notice how it changes your feelings and behaviors.
Daily affirmations: Read your secure beliefs daily. Say them out loud. Write them. Make them real.

modules.title: Module 3 • Emotional Regulation: Managing Relationship Anxiety
modules.overview: Anxious attachment creates intense emotions: fear, anxiety, sadness, anger. This module teaches you to regulate these emotions effectively, so they don't control your behavior. You'll learn mindfulness, distress tolerance, and emotional regulation techniques that help you stay calm and grounded in relationships. When you can regulate your emotions, you can respond instead of react. You can communicate clearly instead of anxiously. You can be present instead of panicked.
takeaways: Emotions are information, not commands: you can feel anxious without acting anxiously.
Regulation is a skill: you can learn to manage intense emotions effectively.
Mindfulness creates space: between feeling and reacting, you can choose your response.
Self-soothing is essential: you can calm yourself without relying on others.
exercises: Anxiety awareness: This week, notice when anxiety appears. What triggers it? How does it feel in your body? What thoughts come with it?
Mindfulness practice: Practice 5 minutes of mindfulness daily. Notice your thoughts and feelings without judgment.
Distress tolerance: When anxiety hits, practice riding the wave. Breathe. Ground yourself. Wait. Notice what happens.
homework: Emotion log: Track your emotions this week. What triggers them? How do you respond? What helps regulate them?
Mindfulness practice: Daily mindfulness for 5–10 minutes. Build the skill. Notice how it affects your anxiety.
Distress tolerance practice: When anxiety appears, practice distress tolerance techniques. Don't act on the anxiety. Ride the wave.
Emotional communication: Practice communicating emotions effectively. Use 'I' statements. Share feelings without blame.

modules.title: Module 4 • Secure Communication: Expressing Needs Without Anxiety
modules.overview: Anxious attachment often leads to anxious communication: indirect, needy, or overwhelming. This module teaches you to communicate needs directly, clearly, and securely. You'll learn to express needs without anxiety, ask for reassurance when appropriate, and communicate in ways that invite connection rather than push partners away. Secure communication builds trust. Anxious communication erodes it. This module helps you choose secure communication.
takeaways: Secure communication is direct, clear, and respectful: it invites connection.
Needs are valid: expressing them directly is healthy, not needy.
Timing matters: choose the right time and place for important conversations.
Listening is as important as speaking: understanding your partner builds connection.
exercises: Communication audit: Review recent communications. Which were anxious? Which were secure? What patterns do you notice?
Need expression practice: Identify 3 needs. Practice expressing them securely. Write them down. Say them out loud.
Active listening practice: In your next conversation, practice active listening. Reflect back. Ask questions. Notice the impact.
homework: Communication practice: This week, practice secure communication. Express needs directly. Ask for reassurance appropriately.
Need expression: Identify one need. Express it securely to your partner or practice expressing it. Notice the response.
Active listening: Practice active listening in conversations. Give full attention. Reflect back. Ask questions.
Difficult conversation: If there's a difficult topic, practice having it securely. Use the framework. Notice what works.

modules.title: Module 5 • Boundaries and Self-Care: Maintaining Your Sense of Self
modules.overview: Anxious attachment often leads to losing yourself in relationships. This module teaches you to set boundaries, maintain your identity, and care for yourself while in relationships. You'll learn that boundaries aren't walls—they're gates. They protect you while allowing connection. You'll learn to balance relationship needs with personal needs. When you maintain your sense of self, you're more secure in relationships. You don't need constant reassurance because you know who you are, with or without a partner.
takeaways: Boundaries protect you and your relationships: they're essential for secure attachment.
You can be close and independent: intimacy and autonomy can coexist.
Self-care isn't selfish: it's essential for healthy relationships.
Your identity matters: maintain it even in relationships.
exercises: Boundary audit: What boundaries do you have? Which are healthy? Which need work? Where do you lose yourself?
Identity check: Who are you outside your relationship? What interests? What goals? What values? Write them down.
Self-care plan: Create a self-care plan. What will you do daily? Weekly? How will you protect it?
homework: Boundary setting: Identify one boundary you need. Set it this week. Communicate it. Enforce it. Notice how it feels.
Identity maintenance: This week, do one thing that's just for you. A hobby. A friend. A goal. Maintain your identity.
Self-care practice: Implement your self-care plan. Daily practices. Weekly practices. Protect them. Notice the impact.
Need balancing: Practice balancing your needs with your partner's. Communicate. Negotiate. Find solutions together.

modules.title: Module 6 • Self-Compassion: Building Inner Security
modules.overview: Self-compassion is the foundation of secure attachment. When you're compassionate with yourself, you don't need constant external validation. You have inner security. This module teaches you to treat yourself with kindness, especially when you're struggling. You'll learn that self-compassion isn't self-pity—it's self-care. When you have self-compassion, you're more secure in relationships. You don't need your partner to complete you because you're already whole.
takeaways: Self-compassion is the antidote to anxious attachment: it builds inner security.
You can be kind to yourself even when you struggle: self-compassion doesn't require perfection.
Inner security reduces relationship anxiety: when you're secure in yourself, you're secure in relationships.
Self-compassion is a practice: it takes time and repetition to develop.
exercises: Self-compassion assessment: How compassionate are you with yourself? Rate yourself 1–10. What would make you more compassionate?
Self-compassion break: Practice the self-compassion break. Notice how it feels. What changes?
Compassionate self-talk: Practice speaking to yourself with compassion. Write compassionate statements. Say them out loud.
homework: Self-compassion practice: Practice self-compassion daily this week. Use the self-compassion break. Notice the impact.
Compassionate journal: Journal about struggles with self-compassion. Be kind. Recognize common humanity. Stay mindful.
Inner security building: Practice building inner security. Self-compassion. Self-care. Self-knowledge. Self-trust.
Loving-kindness meditation: Practice loving-kindness meditation daily. Wish yourself and others well. Notice how it feels.

modules.title: Module 7 • Building Secure Attachment: Integration and Maintenance
modules.overview: This final module helps you integrate everything you've learned into a sustainable practice of secure attachment. You'll create a plan for maintaining progress and continuing growth. You'll learn that secure attachment is a journey, not a destination. It requires ongoing practice, but it becomes easier over time. You'll develop confidence in your ability to maintain secure attachment patterns and handle relationship challenges with security and grace.
takeaways: Secure attachment is a practice: it requires ongoing effort, but it becomes easier.
Progress isn't linear: setbacks are normal; return to the basics when they happen.
Support helps: don't do this alone—seek help when needed.
Celebrate progress: acknowledge how far you've come.
exercises: Progress reflection: Reflect on your journey. What have you learned? How have you grown? What's changed?
Maintenance plan: Create a plan for maintaining secure attachment. What will you do daily? Weekly? Monthly?
Future vision: Imagine your future with secure attachment. What does it look like? How do you feel? What's different?
homework: Integration plan: Create a plan for integrating secure attachment into your daily life. What practices will you maintain?
Support network: Identify your support network. Who can you turn to? How will you maintain connections?
Growth goals: Set 3 goals for continued growth. What will you work on? How will you measure progress?
Celebration: Celebrate your progress. Write about it. Share it. Acknowledge how far you've come.

aiSupport.systemPrompt: Help the user apply one concrete module step at a time. Do not diagnose. Escalate urgent safety concerns to emergency care.
